meta.githubCommitMessage: Fix Leaflet zoom retirement and cover trusted navigation during zoom

job.workflow_name: Temporary Trippin CSV and backup browser v2
job.name: browser

steps.name: Run only the pinned hosted portability packet

observation.success: All original eight portability cases and both added trusted user-zoom navigation regressions passed once at retry zero. CJK actual download/file-chooser restore/reload, authored legacy pretty-file restore/reload, malformed UTF-8 preservation and currency rejection assertions remain intact. New regressions observe a trusted Profile click during active public zoom state, then detached/emptied old DOM host, usable replacement zoom, reload and unchanged durable workspace.
observation.failureHistory: Four earlier failed attempts are preserved separately, including actual delayed-zoom stack evidence from attempt 4. Their failures are not overwritten or relabeled.
observation.network: All 18 actual root HTML responses match the pinned unique deployment; no unexpected reads/mutations/WebSockets or page errors. Known fonts/API/weather/tiles remain blocked.
observation.limits: This accepts the scoped browser-client workflows only. Physical touch/pickers, live tiles/weather, Auth/accounts/Redis/public management, bank/providers, AI, storage-quota races and whole-product acceptance remain outside this run.

scenarios: EUR imports append once and explicit USD rejects without changing existing expenses
ambiguous duplicate and explicit blank currency both reject without losing expenses
actual CJK download above two MB restores after a visible profile edit and survives reload
legacy pretty backup above two MB restores and invalid UTF-8 cannot replace its UI or durable state
an active user zoom retires safely on profile navigation and the replacement map remains usable

Direct child exit/close/EOF and original groups are checked. Same-UID Linux browser processes are additionally attributed by the unique owned binary/profile/cache path and kernel starttime; unreadable or uncertain attribution prevents owned-root deletion. This is not a host-wide process inventory.
Registry/browser downloads and allowed public hosted GETs are setup/acceptance network traffic, not a network sandbox. Userspace deadlines cannot interrupt blocked kernel filesystem calls.
